'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**[[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Federal troops]] seize the town of [[Shire Inda Selassie]] from the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] (TPLF) as [[government of Ethiopia|government]] forces advance on the [[Tigray Region]]'s capital [[Mekelle]]. There are conflicting reports of the status of [[Axum]], with both sides claiming to control the town. TPLF leader [[Debretsion Gebremichael]] says his forces will never surrender and calls on all [[Tigrayans]], including children, to mobilize and take up arms. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-54984056 (BBC News)] [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-ethiopia-conflict-axum/leader-of-ethiopias-rebel-tigray-forces-says-axum-town-with-us-idUKKBN27Z10E (Reuters)]
**Thousands of more people flee into [[Sudan]] from [[Ethiopia]]'s Tigray Region, according to international aid workers. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/19/ethiopia-aid-workers-report-chaos-as-thousands-flee-fighting (''The Guardian'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Military history of Australia during the War in Afghanistan|Australian involvement in the War in Afghanistan]]
**The [[Australian Defence Force]]'s special report into [[war crime]]s in [[Afghanistan]] is released to the public, revealing that 39 civilians and prisoners had been [[killed unlawfully]] by [[special forces]] since 2001. [[Chief of the Defence Force (Australia)|Chief of the Defence Force]] [[Angus Campbell (general)|Angus Campbell]] issues an apology to the [[Afghan people]] and promises significant reform. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/nov/19/key-findings-of-the-brereton-report-into-allegations-of-australian-war-crimes-in-afghanistan (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] reports 5,031 new cases, the highest single-day total since the pandemic began. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-11-19/california-covid-19-cases-new-weekly-record-amid-spike (''Los Angeles Times'')]
*****[[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] orders a curfew (limited [[Stay-at-home order|stay-at-home order]]) for all 41 [[List of counties in California|counties]] in the purple tier of the state's Blueprint for a Safer Economy reopening system; these counties include more than 90% of the state population. The order will be in effect from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] beginning November 21. [https://abc7.com/governor-newsom-california-curfew-gavin-los-angeles/8101518/ (KABC-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]]
*****[[Maryland]] reports a record 2,910 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases since the beginning of the [[pandemic]] to 174,733. [https://baltimore.cbslocal.com/2020/11/19/covid-19-latest-maryland-sets-record-for-highest-single-day-number-of-new-cases-with-2910/ (WJZ-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
*****[[Franklin County, Ohio|Franklin County]], [[Ohio]] is elevated to the state's purple-level amid COVID-19 concerns, becoming the first county in the state to do so. [https://local12.com/news/coronavirus/one-county-in-ohio-jumps-to-purple-alert-level-4-in-latest-advisory-franklin-governor-mike-dewine-cincinnati (WKRC-TV)]
*****[[Miami Valley Gaming]] announces that they will change their operating hours due to the statewide curfew imposed by [[Governor of Ohio|Governor]] [[Mike DeWine]]. [https://www.daytondailynews.com/news/miami-valley-gaming-changes-daily-hours-due-to-statewide-curfew/7G52QHEC7RCP5BTJFWHJRGK7OY/ (''Dayton Daily News'')] 
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
*****[[Pennsylvania]] reports a record 7,126 new cases in the last 24 hours, surpassing 7,000 new cases for the first time since the pandemic began. [https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/coronavirus/covid-19-cases-in-pa-surge-to-single-day-record-as-vaccine-could-arrive-soon/2604085/ (WCAU-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
*****[[Texas]] reports a record 12,293 new cases in the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, there are 147,030 active COVID-19 cases across the state. [https://patch.com/texas/downtownaustin/texas-reports-record-12-293-new-coronavirus-cases-230-deaths (Patch.com)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Utah]]
*****[[Utah]] [[Governor of Utah|Governor]] [[Gary Herbert]] issues a new public health order that will no longer require Utahns to limit social gatherings to only people in their households on [[Thanksgiving]], even as the state reports a record 3,968 new cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2020/11/19/governor-herbert-address/ (''The Salt Lake Tribune'')]
****A record 185,759 new cases are reported in the [[United States]], according to [[Johns Hopkins University]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/19/health/us-coronavirus-thursday/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports a record 1,105 new cases in the last 24 hours, bringing the total cases in the province to 42,797 cases. [https://edmontonjournal.com/news/local-news/covid-19-alberta-breaks-single-day-record-with-1105-new-cases-a-second-man-in-his-30s-died-in-the-edmonton-zone (''Edmonton Journal'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]]
*****[[Manitoba]] is expected to tighten their restrictions on stores and social gatherings in an effort to stop the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2020/11/19/manitoba-further-restricts-social-visits-and-store-openings-during-pandemic.html (''Toronto Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] exceeds 100,000 deaths, becoming the fourth country to do so after [[Brazil]], the [[United States]], and [[India]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/mexico-becomes-4th-country-to-hit-100000-covid-19-deaths/2020/11/19/406cb30e-2acf-11eb-9c21-3cc501d0981f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Cluster 5]] 
*****The [[Ministry of Health (Denmark)|health ministry]] stated that a new, mutated strain of the [[coronavirus]] stemming from [[fur farming|mink farm]]s in [[Denmark|the country]] is "most likely" extinct, amid fears that the new strain could compromise [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201119-denmark-says-mutated-coronavirus-from-mink-farms-most-likely-extinct (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****The [[Northern Ireland Executive]] agrees to implement a two-week tougher [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] beginning November 27. All non-essential retail, close contact services, places of worship and cafés will close after being allowed to reopen tomorrow. [https://www.itv.com/news/utv/2020-11-19/stormont-coronavirus-restrictions (ITV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] surpasses two million total COVID-19 cases after a record 23,610 new cases are reported. It also reports a record 463 new fatalities in the last 24 hours. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/11/19/russias-coronavirus-cases-top-2-million-in-new-one-day-record-increase-a72084 (''The Moscow Times'')]
****Russia resumes the [[vaccination]] of new volunteers in an trial for its flagship [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V vaccine]] after a short pause at the end of October. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronovirus-russia-vaccine/russia-resumes-covid-19-vaccine-trial-after-pause-medical-staff-idUKKBN27Z16P (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Albania]]
****The [[Government of Greece|Greek government]] announces a closure of its border crossing with [[Albania]] in [[Krystallopigi]] beginning tomorrow morning and will also test all people entering the [[Greece|country]] through its land borders as part of efforts to contain the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/259343/article/ekathimerini/news/greek-albanian-border-crossing-to-close-as-government-steps-up-covid-19-restrictions (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****The [[Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine]] recommends the owners of three [[Fur farming|mink farm]]s in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] to cull their [[mink]] to halt the potential spread of a mutated form of the [[coronavirus]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/2020/1119/1179132-mink-covid19/ (RTE)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record of 637 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll in the country to 12,088. [https://polandin.com/50872286/covid19-recordbreaking-637-new-fatalities-in-poland-active-cases-rising (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 257 new fatalities and 13,357 new cases in the past 24 hours, taking the nationwide death toll to 10,369 and the total number of cases to 583,510. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-11-19/ukraine-reports-new-daily-high-coronavirus-cases-deaths-minister (''U.S. News & World Report'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Tokyo Metropolitan Government]] reports a new single-day record of 534 new cases and raise its virus alert in the [[Tokyo|prefecture]] to the highest of four levels for the first time since September, indicating that "infections are spreading". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-11-19/tokyo-raises-virus-alert-to-highest-level-after-record?srnd=prognosis (Bloomberg)]
****Japan reports a record 2,388 new cases, according to official figures. It comes as the country is on "maximum alert" and many prefectures such as [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], [[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi]], and [[Hokkaido Prefecture|Hokkaido]] report record numbers of new cases. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japan-on-maximum-alert-after-record-coronavirus-cases-pm-suga (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2020111900780/japan%E2%80%99s-daily-coronavirus-tally-hits-record-2-388.html (Nippon.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] agrees to provide an advance payment to [[pharmaceutical companies]] developing a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in order to secure millions of [[vaccine]]s. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/duterte-allows-advance-payments-covid-19-vaccine (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[South Korea]] reaches a three-month high of 343 cases, bringing the nationwide total to 29,654 cases, according to data from the [[Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency]]. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20201119002251320?section=national/national (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Premier of Victoria|Victoria Premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] announces a closure of [[Victoria (state)|the state's]] border with [[South Australia]] for 48 hours beginning at 11:59 p.m. [[Time in Australia|AEDT]] tonight. The "hard border" between the two states will be replaced by a permit system beginning at midnight on November 21. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-11-19/victorian-premier-daniel-andrews-closes-south-australia-border/12899296 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Marshall Islands]]
****Just days after announcing that the country was free of COVID-19 again after two infected people recovered, the Marshall Islands reports three new cases from a repatriation flight of Marshallese citizens in [[Hawaii]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/430981/marshall-islands-repatriation-group-has-three-covid-cases (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[AstraZeneca]]’s vaccine candidate shows promise in older adults. Late-stage trials are expected to be released by [[Christmas]]. [https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2020-11-19/oxford-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-data-by-christmas (''Los Angeles Times'')]

***A lawsuit is filed against the [[Chicago Police Department]], accusing them of brutally attacking and falsely arresting protesters during demonstrations against the [[Killing of George Floyd|killing]] of [[George Floyd]]. '''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] wins [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], after the state completed its hand recount, making him the first [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] to win the state since [[Bill Clinton]] in [[1992 United States presidential election|1992]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bidens-win-in-georgia-reaffirmed-after-recount/ (CBS News)] 

'''Science and technology'''
*Citing safety concerns, the [[National Science Foundation]] announces that the 57-year-old [[Arecibo Observatory]] in [[Puerto Rico]] will be decommissioned. Earlier this month, a second cable supporting the 900-ton instrument platform snapped. The platform is suspended 450 feet (137 meters) above the fixed radio dish, which is 1,000 feet (305 meters) in diameter. [https://www.nsf.gov/news/news_summ.jsp?cntn_id=301674 (NSF)]
